question.leadin: This emperor gave the "Jewel Voice Broadcast" to announce his country's surrender in World War II.
question.text: Name this emperor of an Asian country that fought against the US in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
question.clue: This leader's Prime Minister was killed by the League of Blood in the May 15th Incident.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
swap.text: During the Edo period, Japan was ruled by this family, for whom the period is also sometimes named. Ieyasu (EE-ay-ah-soo), a member of this family, won the Battle of Sekigahara to begin the Edo period.
swap.clue: This Japanese clan the ruled from Edo. This clan headed the last feudal military government of Japan, and their first shogun was Ieyasu.

question.text: Prior to the Perry Expedition, the only Japanese port that was largely open to foreigners was this city on the southern island of Kyushu. It later became the second city to be hit with an atomic bomb during World War II.
question.clue: Trade between this city and Macau was carried out by non-American "black ships."

swap.text: The battle for this island, home to three Japanese air fields, saw the raising of an American flag on top of its Mount Suribachi.
swap.clue: Mass casualties were inflicted on marines during this battle by troops with flamethrowers in a tunnel system that had gone undetected.

question.text: This daimyo preceded Toyotomi Hideyoshi as the first "great unifier." He was killed in 1582 when his retainer Akechi Mitsuhide ["mit-soo-hee-day"] rebelled against him.
question.clue: This huge fan of the Tanegashima rifle once won a battle by arranging his arquebusiers into three rows.

swap.text: This American ended the policy of seclusion during the Tokugawa Shogunate after sailing into Tokyo harbor with his "Black Ships" and having the Convention of Kanagawa forcibly signed.
swap.clue: This American naval officer who sailed into Tokyo Bay in 1853 in order to open Japan to large-scale international trade.

question.leadin: Name some catalysts for reform in Japanese history, FTPE.
question.text: This Japanese emperor oversaw the creation of the Diet and the modernization of Japan after the end of the Tokugawa Shogunate.
question.clue: The short-lived Ezo Republic and Satsuma Rebellion were both attempts to counter progressive efforts undertaken during this period, which began after the Boshin War.

swap.leadin: This leader officially declared the return of imperial rule until 1868.
swap.text: Name this Japanese emperor whose "restoration" ended the Tokugawa shogunate. His regnal name roughly translates to "Enlightened Rule."
swap.answerHtml: Emperor Meiji [accept Meiji Emperor; accept Meiji the Great; accept Meiji-tenno or Meiji-taitei; accept Mutsuhito]
swap.clue: This man's governing philosophy was outlined in thefive point "Charter Oath" and would lead to the creation of the position of Prime Minister along with a largely powerless parliament.

question.leadin: How many capitals of Japan are there? Only one. Nevertheless, there have been many ancient capitals of Japan.
question.text: This city names a period following the Asuka and was the first Japanese capital built in the Tang Chinese style. It was also the first permanent capital of Japan, before Nagaoka.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.leadin: One World Heritage site in this city was originally designed by the Czech architect, Jan Letzel.
swap.text: The Enola Gay dropped Little Boy on what city, the first target of an atomic bomb in history?
swap.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

question.leadin: Name these Japanese figures from World War II.
question.text: After becoming commander of all Japanese naval forces in 1941, he orchestrated the attack on . He was shot down and killed in 1943, when forces used deciphered intelligence to ambush his convoy.
question.clue: During the reign of Hirohito, this naval leader was opposed to signing the Tripartite Pact. However, he still orchestrated the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor.

swap.leadin: This work's title character marries Lady Aoi before fathering his only child with Akashi's daughter.
swap.text: Name this Heian period work, sometimes called the world's first novel, written by Lady Murasaki.
swap.clue: This work, often called the world's first novel, is an important insight into Heian court life. It features the blank chapter "Vanished into the Clouds" and was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu.

question.leadin: The feudal title daimyo emerged from the office of shugo, which was created by this period's first leader to govern the different provinces of Japan.
question.text: Name this period of feudal Japan ruled by the country's first shogunate founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo after he defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei war.
question.clue: Despite the establishment of a secret police force called the Rokuhara Tandai during this period, the failure to put down akuto rebels during its later days helped contribute to the downfall of this period's government.

swap.leadin: During one of these events, soldiers fought on and around large walls at Iki-no-matsubara, and before these events a letter was sent addressed to the "ruler of a small country."
swap.text: Name these events chronicled by Suenaga, the second of which was repelled by a fleet-crushing "divine wind."
swap.answerHtml: Mongol invasions of Japan [or Yuan invasions of Japan; or Kublai Khan’s invasions of Japan; accept equivalents for invasion like “attack”; prompt on “Chinese invasion of Japan”; prompt on “invasions of Japan”]
swap.clue: During one of these conflicts, an exaggerated 142,000-strong army was defeated at the battle of Hakata Bay.

question.leadin: Answer the following about foreign relations between Japan and the United States.
question.text: This commodore opened Japan to foreign relations. He first arrived in July 1853 and signed the Convention of Kanagawa the following year. His older brother, Oliver, won the battle of Lake Erie in the War of 1812.
question.clue: He built his early record on expeditions against the slave trade, service in the Mexican War, and three years as commander of the Fulton.

swap.leadin: The final battle in this war saw the sinking of the ship carrying the Emperor Antoku, and this war is detailed in the Tale of the Heike.
swap.text: Name this 12th century civil war in Japan fought between the Taira and Minamoto clans, which ended at the naval battle of Dan-no-Ura
swap.clue: Chronicled in the Azuma kagami, the first major battle of this conflict ended with Yorimasa's death by seppuku after he failed to defend Prince Mochihito; that was the battle of the Uji river.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Genpei War.
question.text: The war concluded with this naval battle won by Yoshitsune off Honshu's southern coast, in Shimonoseki Strait. After it, Yoshitsune's older brother, Minamoto Yuritomo, established the Kamakura shogunate.
question.clue: This battle saw Taguchi Shigeyoshi reveal the location of the Emperor's ship, and both the child-emperor Antoku and his grandmother, the widow of Kiyomori, committed suicide.

swap.text: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

question.leadin: Answer the following about ancient legal codes.
question.text: This 645 CE set of policies promulgated in Japan shortly after the death of Prince Shotoku established the Ritsuryo, a strange mix of Legalistic laws and Confucian rhetoric adapted for Japanese conditions.
question.clue: This set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.

swap.leadin: One of these structures is named after the Japanese word for chopsticks, Hashihaka, due to its resemblance to those utensils, and is thought to contain the body of the mythical queen Pimiko.
swap.text: Name these keyhole-shaped megalithic tombs in Japan. The era lasting from roughly the 3rd century to the 6th century is named for them.
swap.clue: A scholarly debate centers on whether two objects with raised left arms found in one of these places depict horse herders or dancers.
